article.dek: The inactive lists are in — Buffalo is down both starting receivers — plus the board's final prices and tonight's line movement.

items.headline: Inactives are in: Buffalo down both starting receivers
paragraphs: The inactive lists landed about 90 minutes before tonight's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, and the game-time calls broke against Buffalo. Wide receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) is out — he went through a pregame workout at SoFi Stadium and still couldn't go. Cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) and defensive lineman Landon Jackson (knee) are out too, joining the already-ruled-out Joshua Palmer (shoulder) and Ed Oliver (knee).

Buffalo's active receivers: Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Greg Dortch, Trent Sherfield Sr., and rookie Skyler Bell, who makes his NFL debut. Rookie cornerback Jalon Kilgore is active for the first time too and could work in the nickel with Damar Hamlin. Cornerback Christian Benford (toe) is back in uniform after missing last week.

The Rams cleared every tag. Safety Quentin Lake (hip) is active after McVay called it minor, Aaron Donald (back) is back in the lineup, and Colby Parkinson and Jaylen Watson are good to go. No surprise inactives for Los Angeles.

items.headline: Quarterback check: the board matches the news
paragraphs: The app's quarterback feed is fresh this evening and matches the reporting. Josh Allen is Buffalo's expected starter, Matthew Stafford is the Rams' expected starter, and neither carries an injury flag on the board.
That's the check that matters on a game-day evening: the starters are confirmed and there's no stale number to fade, no rumor to chase. Bet the game, not the rumor.
items.takeaway: Allen vs. Stafford, confirmed on both sides. Bet the game, not the rumor.

items.headline: Hit Rate is on Buffalo — and the price got better
paragraphs: Hit Rate means the supported pick the app thinks is most likely to win — win probability first, value second. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate. Tonight it's Buffalo on the moneyline, now +154 on DraftKings for the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium.

The honest number: the app evaluates Buffalo's chance at 37.7% against a 39.4% breakeven at +154 — just short, reliability MEDIUM. The price improved from +150 this morning and the card's state is still BET. The model's raw read likes Buffalo better than the market does, but liking a team and the price paying you are two different things. The card chases the win, not the value.
If your book has Buffalo better than +154, that's a better number than the card; if it's worse, tap Check and run your price before you decide.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate chases the win, not the value. Tonight the win is a dog at a better price than this morning.

items.headline: Balanced stays with Buffalo; Value finds nothing
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. It's Buffalo +3.5 at -115 on DraftKings. The app's evaluated chance is 51.5% against a 53.5% breakeven — short, reliability MEDIUM.

Value is always the model's +EV play, and tonight the Value lane is empty again: no offer on the board satisfies the lane's contract. Some evenings the board's honest answer is nothing. That's the report, not a failure — a quiet board is information too.
items.takeaway: Two cards on Buffalo, both thin; the honest third card is empty.

items.headline: How to use this before kickoff
paragraphs: Every news item above closes the loop the same way. The board refreshes every morning and evening. When your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, or the line moved since the board last refreshed, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One mechanics note: +154 means every $1 you risk wins $1.54; -115 means every $1.15 you risk wins $1. That's price mechanics, not a stake — the app sizes your actual stake from your bankroll and your staking setting, which is deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Report the news first, then use it: Check is how news becomes a number.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine you bet a team at -3 early in the week, and by kickoff the line has moved to -4.5. Even before the game is played, you got a better price than the market's final answer — that is called closing line value, or CLV.

Why it matters: the closing line is usually the sharpest number of the week, because it has seen every injury report and every bet. Beating it consistently is how bettors know they are on the right side of the number over time — one game proves nothing, but the pattern does.

Our Fade rule needs a verified public-vs-sharper split plus corroboration before it becomes a play. I checked the free VSiN splits row tonight: it showed a CFL game, not an NFL game, so no split qualified. When a real one does, this section will say so plainly.
items.takeaway: Beat the closing number often enough and you are probably beating the market — the wins take care of themselves.

items.headline: The total climbed a full point; Buffalo's price ticked up
paragraphs: The one real move today: the DraftKings total went from 54.5 to 55.5, now matching FanDuel and Pinnacle at 55.5. That's a full point of movement on the total — the board caught it.

Elsewhere it's juice, not line. Buffalo's moneyline went from +150 to +154 on DraftKings, and the +3.5 spread juice drifted from -118 back to -115. FanDuel's Buffalo moneyline actually shortened to +148, and Pinnacle's Buffalo price is +160. The line itself never moved — 3.5 stood still all day.
If your book has a different total or a better Buffalo price than the card, tap Check and run your number.
items.takeaway: Totals moved a point; spreads didn't move at all. Shop the number you can bet.

items.headline: Inactives are final, prices are set — one Check
paragraphs: Tonight's card: Buffalo +154 on the moneyline and +3.5 at -115 on the spread at DraftKings. The questionable tags resolved with the inactives — Buffalo is down both starting receivers while the Rams cleared everyone. The model's expected margin has Buffalo about two points better than the spread implies, but the app's evaluated chances still sit just under breakeven.
That's the evening brief: the news is reported, the board has the numbers, and your book's price is the only one that matters. Run it through Check before kickoff.
items.takeaway: One game, final prices, one Check.
